name: lightning_manual
title: Lightning sequence tagger with a hand-rolled gradient update
origin: written alongside ANA-7 to exercise MLV706, MLV707 and MLV711 (Sprint 4)
tunedWhy: the rules were developed against this project, so its numbers are a ceiling, not a measurement - it is excluded from the unseen headline in ACCURACY.md
note: No `graph` block: added for its findings, not for a hand-drawn diagram.

expected.defect: training_step back-propagates by hand while automatic optimization is still on
expected.why: Lightning calls backward again after the hook returns, so the gradients are applied twice per batch and the effective learning rate is silently doubled

expected.defect: a OneCycleLR is returned from configure_optimizers with no {"interval": "step"}
expected.why: Lightning steps a returned scheduler once per epoch, so the whole cycle completes in the first ten batches and the rest of training runs at the floor learning rate

expected.defect: ProbeLit.training_step logs its loss and returns nothing
expected.why: Lightning back-propagates whatever the hook returns, so every batch of the probe is skipped and the loss curve is flat with no error to explain it

forbidden.why: the checkpoint round-trip is the safe one: torch.save(model.state_dict(), ...) and torch.load(..., map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
the OneCycleLR is never stepped by hand at all - configure_optimizers only declares it, and there is no loop here to judge a cadence against
pl.seed_everything(SEED, workers=True) at line 27 and an explicit generator on the split
the validation DataLoader is built with shuffle=False
Lightning owns the eval loop; validation_step is the hook, and model.eval() is the Trainer's job
